> 乾。元亨，利貞。

This is the first hexagram, and the one whose name is most often turned into a mood: heaven, yang, pure force, the sky.

The character does not say that.

## 乾 began as a picture of the sun coming up

乾's original form is 倝, built on 日 — the sun. The image is sunrise, with a banner's shadow swinging as the light rises. 乾 is the later differentiated character.

說文: 乾，上出也 — "up and out." Two characters that match the picture exactly: the sun going up.

So 乾 is ascending energy — the motion of rising and initiating. Not a static sky. The rising is written into the form.

(And a caution the book insists on: 乾 is not "built from 乙." That reading comes from the small-seal form, not from the oracle-bone structure.)

## 元 is a head

甲骨 元 is a 一 above 兀 — 兀 being a person seen from the side, and the 一 marking the head. The original sense is head.

說文 glosses 元 as 始, beginning — a natural extension: the head is where a body begins.

But the 彖's 大哉乾元，萬物資始 is not "everything starts from it" in the sense of a starting point in time. It is: everything has its beginning by means of it. A point on a timeline versus a root.

## 貞 is a question, not a virtue

貞 shares its oracle-bone form with 卜 — it is the character for the act of divining.

說文 is accurate here: 貞，卜問也 — to ask by divination.

Later it means "to hold firm," and that is the result of asking: what has been asked accurately can be kept.

So 利貞 is not the moral sentence "it is beneficial to be upright." It is: beneficial in what was asked. Which is exactly the knot the 系辭 has to untie when it turns a divination book into a book about the way.

## 亢 is a neck

亢 depicts the neck. 說文: 亢，人頸也.

The neck is the most exposed part of a body: the head is held up by it, the throat passes through it.

So 亢龍有悔 is not "the dragon at the height." It is the dragon stretching its neck upward — and one more stretch would break it.

## 用九：見群龍無首

首 is the head — and the point of using that word is that the head is the one part of a body there is only one of.

Among many dragons, a 首 would mean a unique one. 無首 is: there is no single one.

Which is not chaos. It is the condition in which no member has become the standard the others are measured against.

## 各正性命，保合太和

The 彖's sequence is the chapter's real content: 乾道變化，各正性命，保合太和，乃利貞.

Each thing's nature and life are set right first; only then is the great harmony preserved.

So 太和 is not an agreement reached by smoothing differences. It is what holds after each thing has been set in its own place. Harmony bought by erasing the difference is what this book calls 合 — the manufactured join — and it is what 太和 is not.

## A test

Take one thing you are currently pushing upward — a project, a claim, a position. Ask where the neck is: the part that is now taking the whole weight of the head. 亢 is not a height; it is a posture.
